_comment: The schema, declared once, read by both the profiler and the migration.
Point this at your own tables and the whole kit follows: the SELECT and
INSERT statements, the per-type conversions, and which checks the
verification suite runs.
The type is what does the work. It decides three things at once:
- how the value is read out of SQL Server (uuid needs a CAST)
- how it is converted in Python (money must stay Decimal, never float)
- which verification checks apply (money gets summed, dates get
min/max compared, nullable columns get NULL counts)
Supported types:
int, bigint   whole numbers
text          NVARCHAR / VARCHAR / text
char          fixed width, trailing-space semantics preserved
money         MONEY / numeric(19,4). Compared exactly, never rounded
bool          BIT / boolean
uuid          UNIQUEIDENTIFIER / uuid. Migrated as a STRING, because
SQL Server stores the first three fields little-endian
and moving raw bytes scrambles the value
timestamp     DATETIME2 / timestamptz. Read as source_timezone
date          DATE. No timezone on either side
generated     computed on the target. Never inserted, only verified
Tables must be listed parents-first: the migration loads in this order
and truncates in reverse, so foreign keys hold at both ends.
_source_timezone_comment: DATETIME2 carries no timezone, so this is an assertion about the
application that wrote the data, not something the database can tell
you. Get it wrong and every timestamp shifts by the offset, which moves
dates across midnight and changes which day a settlement belongs to.
The date_ranges check exists to catch exactly that.

_comment: Optional. Names a column whose values differ only by case, and the
value a real query filters on.
SQL Server's default collation is case-insensitive and PostgreSQL is
not, so the same WHERE clause returns different rows on each side with
no error. Set this and the suite measures the gap instead of leaving
it to be discovered in production.
Optional. Substrings that must survive the load byte-for-byte.
Encoding damage shows up in no row count and no sum.
